satellyte.outcome: Turns public buying signals into enriched, scored leads for B2B revenue teams.

cover.alt: Satellyte lead table with scores, signal badges, and pipeline status on dummy data

screenshots: Radars watch LinkedIn for buying signals that match a target profile.
Describe the ideal customer once: job titles, locations, industries, and company size.
Pick which behaviour counts as intent: posts, hiring, funding, job changes, or competitors.
Every lead arrives scored and tagged with the signal that surfaced it.
One timeline per lead: what triggered it and what was done about it.
See who else decides at the same company, grouped by seniority.

overview: Satellyte is an AI-powered B2B sales intelligence platform. It watches public buying signals, turns them into scored leads with contact data already attached, and pushes those leads into the tools a revenue team already uses.
features: Signal radars that run 10+ buying-signal strategies continuously in the background.
A lead workspace showing score, signal type, source radar, location, and status for every lead.
Multi-provider contact enrichment with fallbacks, so one provider failing does not empty the result.
AI discovery: describe the company or person you want in plain language and get matching results.
Company view that lists decision-makers by seniority and can go find more of them.
Integrations with Slack, HeyReach, and Instantly, plus a custom webhook API.
LinkedIn engagement automation and AI-assisted content workflows.
Credit-metered public REST API, Stripe billing with idempotent webhooks, and Docker/GHCR delivery.
responsibilities: Built the Next.js product interface, from the radar and lead workspaces to the settings surface.
Built the Fastify services, the BullMQ signal engine, and the background jobs behind every long-running task.
Orchestrated the enrichment providers behind one normalized workflow with fallbacks.
Built the browser automation layer, including per-account safety limits.
Built the public API, its credit metering, authentication, and rate limiting.
Owned production delivery through Docker, GHCR, and GitHub Actions.

palmgrade.outcome: Grades palm fruit from three live industrial camera feeds and surfaces results to operators in real time.

cover.alt: AutoGrade live grading console with three camera lines, bunch counts, and ripe rate on demo data

screenshots: Three conveyor lines graded live: bunch counts, ripe rate, scale weight, and the truck being unloaded.
The same live view in dark mode, with today's grading results filling up below.
Every bunch keeps its photo and grade; tap a thumbnail to open it full size.
A four-stage weighbridge board: arrived, unloading, weighed out, and done, with net weight per truck.
A recap per truck: bunches, the ripe, unripe, JK, and TP split, ripe rate, and net weight, with CSV download.
Registered trucks with supplier and source, internal or external, plus QR printing for scanning.

overview: AutoGrade grades palm fruit as it passes three production camera feeds, and puts the result in front of factory operators while the batch is still on the line.
features: Live inference on three camera feeds at once, using YOLO, OpenCV, and TensorRT behind a FastAPI service.
Operator dashboard covering all three production lines, updated live over Server-Sent Events.
AI capture viewer for reviewing exactly what the model saw on a graded batch.
Role-based access separating operators from supervisors.
Offline-tolerant event delivery: local buffering and batch sync with UUID idempotency keys, so a retry never duplicates a reading.
Weighbridge tickets in four steps with gross, tare, and net weight per truck visit, plus recaps per day and per truck with CSV export.
responsibilities: Built the Python inference service around the vision models and the camera pipeline.
Built the TypeScript API, the event path, and the role-based access rules.
Built the Next.js operator dashboard and the AI capture viewer.
Designed the buffering and synchronization strategy for unstable factory connectivity.
Packaged the stack as versioned containers for deployment inside the plant.

autoerp.outcome: Turns every weighed and graded truck into a priced ticket, a stock receipt, and a daily yield report.

cover.alt: AutoERP mill summary with document shortcuts, yield cards, and daily charts on dummy data

screenshots: One screen for the whole mill: document shortcuts, fruit received, purchase value, and daily yield.
Weighbridge tickets with status, truck, net weight, and value; tickets still waiting sit next to finalised ones.
A finalised ticket: gross, tare, net, quality deduction, price per kilogram, and the AutoGrade result.
Grading breakdown per criterion with weight, and the link to the purchase receipt it created.
The purchase receipt created from the ticket, with the quantity taken from the net weight.
Yield per day: fruit processed against the crude palm oil and kernel produced.

overview: AutoERP is an ERP for palm oil mills, built as a custom module on Frappe and ERPNext. It picks up where the weighbridge and AutoGrade leave off: each truck visit becomes a priced ticket, the ticket posts its own stock receipt, and production is reported as daily oil and kernel extraction rates.
features: Weighbridge tickets with gross, tare, and net weight for every truck visit.
Quality deduction and price per kilogram calculated from the AutoGrade bunch result.
Purchase receipts created automatically when a ticket is finalised, linked back to the ticket.
Daily production entries and an extraction rate report for crude palm oil and kernel.
A mill summary with document shortcuts, key numbers, and trend charts.
Role profiles for mill staff and an Indonesian interface.
responsibilities: Built the mill module on Frappe and ERPNext: doctypes, workflows, and reports.
Connected AutoGrade results to the weighbridge ticket and its pricing rules.
Automated the ticket-to-receipt posting into ERPNext stock.
Built the extraction rate report and the mill summary.
Packaged the stack with Docker for deployment.

ujigo.outcome: Helps distance-learning university students practise timed exams, review every answer, and drill their mistakes.

cover.alt: UjiGo answer review with the score, the correct answer, and its explanation on dummy data

Choose Study mode with instant explanations, or a timed Exam mode.

An instant pass or fail result with the score and a shortcut to retry wrong answers.

A daily dashboard with streak, average score, quick actions, and weak areas.
An XP leaderboard with leagues, streaks, and accuracy.

features: A practice exam bank per course and study program, with free and paid sets.
Study mode with instant explanations, and an exam mode with a timer and copy protection.
Autosaved progress, a question navigator, and instant scoring.
A review page with the correct answer and an explanation for every question.
A mistake book that brings wrong answers back on a spaced-repetition schedule.
Dashboard, streaks, XP, and leaderboards that keep students coming back.
Paid plans through Midtrans.
responsibilities: Built the exam flow end to end in Next.js: question bank, exam session, scoring, and review.
Modelled courses, attempts, and the mistake book in PostgreSQL with Prisma.
Built the spaced-repetition schedule, progress tracking, and the leaderboard.
Integrated Midtrans payments for the paid plans.
Built the dashboard, streaks, and XP system.

production-tracking.outcome: Follows every box of parts from a printed lot card through each station scan to a live monitoring board.

cover.alt: Production Tracking monitoring board with lot counts per station and a lot table on dummy data

Full traceability per lot, from card creation to assembly.
A shop-floor board showing the shift target against live machine output.

overview: Production Tracking follows parts through a factory one box at a time. Each box gets a printed lot card, every station scans the card in and out, and supervisors watch a live board that shows where each lot is, how long it has waited, and which lots are stuck.

Station scan kiosks with a full-screen in or out confirmation, by scanner or camera.
A monitoring board with lot counts per station, subcontract status, and lots waiting too long.
An append-only scan history per lot, where a wrong scan is reversed instead of deleted.
A machine counter board comparing the shift target with actual output.

Built the QR and barcode card layouts for label printers.
Built the machine counter display for the shop floor.

overview: E-Passport is a mobile web app for event attendees. Organizers run the event, booths, quizzes, and rewards from an admin CMS. The screenshots here run on an invented demo event.
features: Phone number sign-in with a lookup that fills in the attendee from the participant list.
Booth activities with quizzes and a one-time PIN check-in from the booth rep.
Progress kept on the server, with the event kit unlocked only when every booth is done.
A reward claim released by a rep's PIN, once per day.
Symposium sessions with time and room, next to the booths.
An admin CMS for events, booths, quiz questions, menu items, and rewards.
responsibilities: Built most of my share in the admin CMS: event, booth, quiz, and reward management.

Built screens in the Next.js attendee app.
Worked in a small team across the attendee app, the API, and the CMS.
